_README: Error rates for the rules that decide what the Index publishes. Each was measured against a hand-judged sample drawn by seeded shuffle; `npm run validate -- --full` redraws the same samples. Intervals are Wilson 95%.

overExclusion.how: full census of every withdrawn domain; homepage fetched, title and description read by hand

underExclusion.how: `npm run probe-filter` — seed 2026, 66 kept domains drawn. A domain is called unreadable only after three surfaces give nothing: homepage with the auditor's bot UA, the same request with a browser UA, then robots.txt and sitemap.xml, whose URL paths name what a site is made of. A non-200 body at that last step is an error page, not evidence, and counts as unresolved. Body text scanned for adult, gambling and piracy vocabulary; every hit hand-judged.
underExclusion.flagged: 7 hits, all hand-rejected: gmx.net and libero.it (portal 'Jackpot' is casual browser games), infobae.com (an OnlyFans obituary headline), polybuzz.ai (its own FAQ saying it bans public NSFW), asus.com ('slots' = memory slots), nine.com.au (a bingo-hall burglary story), xe.com (XXX is the ISO 4217 code for no currency).

wholePopulationBound.how: assume every domain that stayed unreadable is a wrong keep. 5 of 66 — britishairways.com, discogs.com, viator.com, lowes.com, allegro.pl — answer automated clients with a Cloudflare or Akamai wall.
wholePopulationBound.says: at the far edge of the interval, at most 16.5% of kept domains are wrongly kept. This is the bound that faces the whole drawn sample, not just the part that could be read.

underExclusion.tiers: 48 judged on page body, 13 on robots/sitemap only, 5 on nothing. If the 13 robots/sitemap judgements are not trusted either, the worst case becomes 18/66 = 27.3%, 95% CI 18.0-39.0%.
underExclusion.supersedes: 0/44 readable, CI 0-8.0%, which covered the readable population only and left a third of the sample unmeasured. Same seed, same draw; the difference is that unreadable domains were pursued on other surfaces instead of discarded.
underExclusion.drift: britishairways.com resolved on robots/sitemap in one run and not in the next, so the unresolved count moves between 4 and 5 and the worst-case bound between 14.6% and 16.5%. The more conservative run is what is published. Re-running the command reprints the tier counts, so a drift of this kind shows up rather than hiding inside a single number.

inSample.how: seed 42, 15 sites x 4 categories — the set the rule was tuned against, so not evidence of accuracy

heldOut.how: seed 99, disjoint from seed 42, 10 readable sites x 4 categories
heldOut.note: SUPERSEDED as the current rate by heldOutPostFix. Retained because it is what the rule scored before clarin.com and grow.google were fixed.

heldOutPostFix.how: seed 777, disjoint from seeds 42 and 99; 14 readable sites x 4 categories, judged by hand
heldOutPostFix.note: measured after the clarin.com and grow.google fixes. Pre-fix on seed 99 the held-out rate was 10%.
heldOutPostFix.checked: mega.nz 0/20 and bankofamerica.com 5/20 looked like under-credits and were verified correct: mega.nz serves a one-word JS shell, bankofamerica.com links no privacy page from its homepage HTML.

falsePositive.note: three detections is too few to support a rate; each was hand-checked against platform runtime config, not the detector's own patterns

shopMembership.how: seed 11, 20 domains marked shop, judged by hand
shopMembership.boundary: A shop is a site whose primary purpose is selling goods or services to the public and where a visitor can start a purchase. News, reference, social, government, sport, banking and free tools are not shops even when they sell a subscription. Whether to narrow this to retail only is a product decision, not a measurement one.
